Content the engine's own tests load and render.

`assets/` is a content root in the same shape a game's is -- the runtime host
run from this directory mounts it by default -- and it holds only what engine
tests need: the golden-image scenes, the render benches, the lighting spikes,
and a scene with nothing in it. None of it names a game component or a
gameplay vocabulary, so a test game that registers nothing can load it. That is
the point: a fixture that needs a particular game module to be loadable makes
the test about that module.

The `dev/` materials, mesh, and texture are the same handful the template
ships, copied rather than shared so this root stands on its own.

`assets/.cooked/`, `assets/asset_ids.json`, and the skinned rig under
`assets/meshes/dev/` are regenerated by the tests and are not committed.

`project.senchaproj` lets the editor cook these scenes (the skinned goldens go
through the editor, which is the process composed with every asset store). Its
game module is the render host from the default in-tree build; the editor only
borrows a module's component serializers, and this content names none, so a
build elsewhere still opens the project with a "failed to load game module"
line and cooks the same bytes.
